title: High and low tide at a dock

stimulus.title: Depth of water at a dock
stimulus.html: The depth of water at the end of a dock changes with the tide. On one day, high tide, with a depth of 3.1 meters, occurs at 2 a.m., and the next low tide, with a depth of 0.7 meters, occurs at 8 a.m. The sinusoidal function WW models the depth of the water, in meters, tt hours after midnight. In this model, high tides are 12 hours apart. The graph of WW for 2≤t≤142 \le t \le 14 is shown with its axes unscaled. The points PP, QQ, RR, SS and TT are on the graph: PP and TT are highest points, RR is a lowest point, and QQ and SS are on the midline.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points PP, QQ, RR, SS and TT.

rubric.point: The extremes: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P = (2, 3.1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = (8, 0.7)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T = (14, 3.1)</annotation></semantics></math>

The midline points: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q = (5, 1.9)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S = (11, 1.9)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: High tide at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and low tide at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math> are half a cycle apart, so the period is 12 hours and the points are 3 hours apart. The midline is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3.1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3.1 + 0.7}{2} = 1.9</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P = (2, 3.1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q = (5, 1.9)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R = (8, 0.7)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S = (11, 1.9)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T = (14, 3.1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The function WW is given by W(t)W(t)=acos⁡(b(t+c))+d= a\cos(b(t + c)) + d, where aa, bb, cc and dd are constants. Find values of aa, bb, cc and dd.

accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = -\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> with a matching <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that fit the graph: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -2</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = -1.2</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -8</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 4</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: any <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that differs from these by a multiple of 12

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3.1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = \frac{3.1 + 0.7}{2} = 1.9</annotation></semantics></math> and the amplitude is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3.1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3.1 - 0.7}{2} = 1.2</annotation></semantics></math>. The time from high to low tide, 6 hours, is half a period, so the period is 12 hours and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. A cosine with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> is highest where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t + c = 0</annotation></semantics></math>; high tide is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(t - 2)\right) + 1.9</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is WW increasing or decreasing on the interval (8,11)(8, 11)? Give a reason for your answer in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: Increasing, with a reason: after low tide at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math> the water rises toward the next high tide
accept: the depth goes from 0.7 m at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> up to 1.9 m at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 11)</annotation></semantics></math>: low tide is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, and from then the water rises, reaching the midline depth 1.9 m at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 11</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is the rate of change of WW increasing or decreasing on the interval (8,11)(8, 11)? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: Increasing, with a reason: the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 11)</annotation></semantics></math> (below the midline, between the lowest point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> and the midline point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: the water rises faster and faster after low tide
the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing because the graph is concave up

parts.sample: The rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 11)</annotation></semantics></math>. Just after low tide the depth barely changes; the graph is below its midline and concave up there, so the water rises faster and faster until <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 11</annotation></semantics></math>.
